tldr: Fastest to Seoul: AREX Express, non-stop to Seoul Station in ~43 min.
Before leaving arrivals, do it in this order: cash → SIM/eSIM → T-money (stores take won only).
No Korean needed for taxis — Kakao T, Uber, and the official International Taxi all support foreigners.
Incheon has Terminal 1 & 2 (different airlines), linked by a free shuttle; Gimpo is closer to the city.

highlights.title: AREX Express is the fastest to Seoul Station
highlights.body: Non-stop from either Incheon terminal to Seoul Station in about 43 minutes (51 from Terminal 2). The all-stop train is cheaper; airport buses drop closer to many hotels.

highlights.title: Do three things before you leave arrivals — in order
highlights.body: 1) Get some cash (exchange booth or ATM). 2) Buy a SIM/eSIM. 3) Buy a T-money card. This order matters because airport convenience stores sell T-money for cash (won) only.

highlights.title: Foreigner-friendly taxis exist
highlights.body: Kakao T (English/Japanese, foreign-card option), Uber, and the official International Taxi (fixed fares, certified English/Japanese/Chinese drivers) all work for visitors — see the taxi-apps section below.

arrival.title: Your arrival at Incheon, step by step
arrival.intro: From wheels-down to on your way into the city — the exact order that saves time.
arrival.imgAlt: Arrivals hall at Incheon International Airport Terminal 1
arrival.credit: Photo: Wikimedia Commons contributor · CC BY 4.0

steps.title: Connect to free Wi-Fi
steps.detail: Join 'Incheon Airport WiFi' (no password) so you can use maps and messaging right away.

steps.title: Immigration
steps.detail: Have your passport ready plus your e-Arrival Card (or K-ETA if it applies to you). Fingerprints and a photo may be taken.

steps.title: Baggage & customs
steps.detail: Collect your bags, then take the green lane (nothing to declare) or the red lane if you carry alcohol, tobacco, or goods worth over about US$800.

steps.title: Get some cash
steps.detail: Currency-exchange booths and ATMs sit between baggage claim and the exit. Grab around ₩100,000 to start — you'll need won for T-money.

steps.title: SIM or eSIM
steps.detail: Telecom counters (e.g. LG U+) are in the arrivals hall; setup takes ~10–15 min and your phone must be unlocked. An eSIM can be activated before you even land.

steps.title: T-money card
steps.detail: Buy and charge it at GS25/CU or the Transportation Center machines (B1). Stores take won only — that's why cash comes first. Load ₩20,000–30,000.

steps.title: Head into the city
steps.detail: Follow 'AREX / Train' signs to B1 for the train, the 'Bus' signs for airport buses, or the marked taxi stand outside.

transport.title: Incheon → Seoul: compare your options
transport.intro: Pick by speed, price, and where you're staying. Exact fares are in the Verified-facts boxes above.

rows.label: AREX All-stop
vals: Cheapest; staying near an AREX station

rows.label: Limousine / airport bus
vals: Drops near many hotels; lots of luggage

transport.note: Fares are volatile — confirm at arex.or.kr or with the operator. AREX runs about 05:20–23:32; plan a bus or taxi for late arrivals.

taxiApps.title: Taxi apps & services for foreigners
taxiApps.intro: You don't need to speak Korean to take a taxi. These are built for — or work well for — foreign visitors:

items.name: Kakao T
items.d: Korea's dominant taxi app (90%+ share), so matching is fast. Book a regular taxi, see the route, and pay the driver by card/cash — or add a non-Korean card under My Info › Payment.

items.name: Uber (UT)
items.d: Dispatches licensed Korean taxis with seamless in-app payment on your foreign card. Smaller fleet, so waits can be longer off-peak or outside big cities.

items.name: TADA / i.M
items.d: Premium van rides (Kia Carnival) with trained drivers — comfortable for groups and luggage, roughly 20–30% above standard fare, mainly in the Seoul area.

items.name: International Taxi
items.d: Official service certified by the Seoul government; drivers pass a language test. Flat, transparent fares and 24/7 booking via its own app/site, with desks in the Incheon arrivals halls.

taxiApps.tip: For the airport run, International Taxi's fixed fare removes any meter/traffic surprise. For everyday city trips, Kakao T matches fastest. Whatever you use, ignore anyone touting rides inside the arrivals hall.

items.d: Airport convenience stores sell T-money for won only — no foreign cards. Exchange or hit an ATM first.
Ignore anyone approaching you inside arrivals offering a ride. Use the official taxi stand, Kakao T, or the International Taxi desk.
Take the red lane for alcohol, tobacco, or goods over ~US$800; otherwise the green lane.

items.t: Wrong terminal on the way back
items.d: Terminal 1 and Terminal 2 serve different airlines. Check yours before departure — the free shuttle between them takes ~15–20 min.
AREX runs until about 23:32. Late arrivals should plan a bus or taxi instead.

items.q: What's the fastest way into Seoul?
items.a: The AREX Express — non-stop to Seoul Station in about 43 minutes — then a short taxi or subway hop to your accommodation.
The AREX all-stop train (up to about ₩5,350) if you're near an AREX station, or a standard airport bus.

items.q: Can I take a taxi without speaking Korean?
items.a: Yes. Kakao T supports English and Japanese, Uber is in English, and the official International Taxi has certified English/Japanese/Chinese drivers with fixed fares.
Different airlines use each terminal; a free shuttle connects them in about 15–20 minutes. Check your airline before you fly.

items.q: Where do I get a SIM and a T-money card?
items.a: Telecom counters and convenience stores in the arrivals hall. T-money needs cash (won), so exchange money first — or set up an eSIM before you land.
Gimpo handles domestic and some short-haul international flights and sits closer to central Seoul, reachable by subway (Line 5/9, AREX) and bus.
